title: Charles V to his ambassadors in England (Simon Renard, "lieutenant d'Amont"), Brussels, 24 January 1554: the cipher passage on Besançon BM Ms 1582, f. 2, with its contemporary decipherment

documents.shelfmark: Bibliothèque municipale de Besançon, Ms 1582, f. 2 (recto and verso)
documents.date: 24 January 1554 (identified from the printed minute; the leaf carries "1555" in a later hand)
documents.route: Charles V (Brussels) -> his ambassadors in England (Lalaing, Egmont, Courrières, Simon Renard)

plaintext.source: Contemporary decipherment around the cipher (full-width lines above and below, and the margin); the minute printed by Gachard (1882) pp. 313-314 and calendared in CSP Spain XII pp. 46-47; Weiss IV pp. 188-192 prints the Besançon copy with a lacuna exactly at this passage.

transcription.source: Claude (Opus 5.5) for Brice Dudout, 18 Nov 2026: two blind passes with the margin masked (1,074 and 1,075 signs, 91 % agreement after name mapping), reconciled sign by sign
transcription.notes: Research scans sent by the Bibliothèque municipale de Besançon on 18 Nov 2026; not reproduced (library's consent needed). The last line of each page (r24, v26) was cut off in the crops and is not transcribed.

system.summary: Charles V's French cipher to Simon Renard, 1549-1554, as published by Pich-Ponce (2024): numbers for letters (a..t = 20..2, a second series 21-39), syllables written as the letter preceding the consonant plus a vowel mark (+ a, bar above e, bar below i, two dots o, dot below u), 66 for et, code signs for persons, nulls.
system.notes: Key re-derived here independently (key.tsv) and found to match Pich-Ponce's published structure; her tables were not compared sign by sign. distinct_symbols = 64 base forms in transcription pass B (139 base+mark combinations).

prior_solution.where: Contemporary decipherment on the leaf; text: Gachard, Voyages des souverains des Pays-Bas IV (1882) pp. 313-314, Tyler, CSP Spain XII (1949) pp. 46-47; key: Pich-Ponce, Cuadernos de Historia Moderna 49 (2024) pp. 27-45; Tomokiyo, Cryptiana (March 2026)

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout asked the Bibliothèque municipale de Besançon for the scans (04 Nov 2026), received them free on 18 Nov 2026, chose to send the result as a verification once the prior art was found; Claude transcribed, aligned, re-derived the key and searched the prior art.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: Scans of Ms 1580 f. 239 and Ms 1582 f. 2 requested from the Bibliothèque municipale de Besançon; received free for research on 18 Nov 2026.
Two blind transcriptions with the margin masked; reconciled sign by sign (transcription/).

Key re-derived by aligning the cipher with the contemporary decipherment on the page; rule base letter + vowel mark fitted; split-page hold-out 0.726 / 0.691 against shuffled keys at most 0.25 (seed alignment used both pages).

Weiss IV no. LXIII (lacuna at this passage), Gachard IV app. CLV (full minute), CSP Spain XII pp. 44-49, Pich-Ponce 2024 (the cipher, published), Cryptiana March 2026: the text and the key are in print.

Decoded cipher compared with the contemporary decipherment and with the printed minute: the minute agrees with the cipher against the decipherment in 21 places, with the decipherment in 1 (divergences_vs_minute.tsv); key structure matches Pich-Ponce 2024.
358 words: 210 sure, 125 probable, 4 restored, 19 in two lines not transcribed (reading.md).

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: Decode of the cipher with a key re-derived here from the leaf's own contemporary decipherment (EM alignment of the blind transcription with the decipherment written around the cipher), checked against the minute printed by Gachard (1882); the key's structure matches the cipher published by Pich-Ponce (2024), found afterwards.
outcome.fraction_read_source: reading.md: 210 sure of 358 words (repository rule, sure words only); with probable words 335/358 = 0.936

gaps.item: r24 and v26 (last line of each page)
gaps.detail: the two lines are on the library's scans we hold but fell outside the crops used for the two blind passes; not transcribed in this folder (no outside blocker); about 19 words, known from the minute (Gachard IV pp. 313-314) and counted as not read

gaps.item: key gaps (no/po, nz d/i, w a/l, mt/nt n/p)
gaps.detail: left open in the re-derived key.tsv; the cipher's own table is in print (Pich-Ponce 2024, tables printed as images), so these values are not unknown, only not transferred; matching her printed sign shapes to our sign names on the leaf was not done here (her article is not in our files)

gaps.item: physical link with Ms Granvelle 73 ff. 119-122
gaps.detail: hypothesis that f. 2 was detached from the copy Weiss printed with a lacuna; not checked

outcome.notes: No image of the Bibliothèque municipale de Besançon is reproduced. The library dates the leaf 1555; the text is the letter of 24 Jan 1554.

texts.label: Ms 1582, f. 2r-v: Charles V to his ambassadors in England, 24 Jan 1554 (cipher passage)
texts.summary: Charles V tells his ambassadors in London how to answer the French peace overtures: he has always wanted peace, the French broke the truce of their own will, his proposal of September 1553 made at the request of the Cardinal of Imola (Dandino) was never answered; he will negotiate through Mary Tudor once French terms for peace or truce are known; Renard is to learn from Paget what the French ambassador said about marriage matches.
